ambiguities.description: Vendor addresses: the transcript mentions three distinct addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) that are 'frequently different and frequently wrong', but no fact types or structure were captured for them since detail wasn't pursued. Should each address type be modeled as a separate fact type/value type (e.g., Vendor has RemitToAddress), and should addresses be structured (street/city/etc.) rather than a single text value?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: RiskReview 'current' flag: it's stated a vendor accumulates multiple review records over time, at most one of which is 'current'. This requires either a boolean/derived 'is current' attribute or a distinct current-review relationship, which was not fully modeled as a separate fact/constraint. How should 'current' be represented and enforced (e.g., a CurrentReview subtype or flag with an internal uniqueness per vendor)?

source_references.excerpt: A vendor can have several reviews over its life -- we re-review on a cycle, and every re-review is a new record, we don't edit the old one. But one of them is the current signed-off one.

ambiguities.description: The 'RiskReview is for Vendor' mandatory constraint was stated as applying only to active vendors, not all vendors ('Every active vendor has a current signed-off risk review. Draft vendors have none.'). This is a conditional mandatory constraint dependent on VendorStatus = 'active', which cannot be cleanly expressed as a simple mandatory constraint without a subtype (e.g., ActiveVendor) or a more complex rule. How should this conditional mandatory participation be formally modeled?

source_references.excerpt: Every _active_ vendor has a current signed-off review. A draft vendor has no review at all -- that's the normal case, that's what draft means.

ambiguities.description: Vendor transition to 'active' status requires a completed, signed-off risk review as a precondition (a state-transition / dynamic rule), which is a business rule not directly expressible as a static ORM constraint on the fact types as modeled. Should this be captured as a derivation rule or a documented business process constraint outside the static schema?

source_references.excerpt: But the system does enforce it -- you cannot move a vendor to active without a completed review, the transition is blocked.

ambiguities.description: Tier terminology overload: both procurement and compliance call their classification 'tier', causing confusion, though the system stores them as two distinct fields (SpendTier and RiskTier as modeled here). Should the object model enforce naming to avoid ambiguity in reports/UI even though the underlying fields are already separate?

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it 'tier'. ... We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos.

ambiguities.description: Duplicate vendor records: the transcript indicates vendors can be onboarded twice by accident, creating duplicate entities that should represent the same real-world supplier, and there's a two-year-old unresolved cleanup project. This is flagged as out of scope but represents a potential data-quality/identity issue not resolved by the vendor_number identifier scheme.

source_references.excerpt: we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them. ... The duplicates are a real problem. There's a cleanup project that's been on the roadmap for two years.

ambiguities.description: Post-suspension handling of in-flight Purchase Orders is explicitly undecided (a possible 'run-off' status was proposed but not agreed). No fact type or constraint should be added for this until the steering group decides; flagging so it is not silently omitted from future model versions.

source_references.excerpt: Parking it explicitly: what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' concept (Mei's spreadsheet column indicating which vendor to prefer when multiple can supply the same item) is explicitly ad hoc with no defined rule or criteria, and was explicitly excluded from modeling by the stakeholder. Confirming it should remain excluded unless a defined rule emerges.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called 'preferred.' It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. It's not in the system anywhere. ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: Region count/enumeration: Region is modeled as an entity type with RegionCode as identifier and also given a value_constraint of four fixed codes (EMEA, APAC, NA, LATAM), but there is mention that EMEA may be split in the future, suggesting the enumeration is not fully stable. Should RegionCode be a fixed value constraint or should Region remain an open entity without a hardcoded value list?

source_references.excerpt: Four regions, fixed? ... Four today. There's been talk of splitting EMEA but it hasn't happened.

ambiguities.description: Contact uniqueness/identification: Contact was inferred to need its own identifier (contact_id) since a vendor can have multiple contacts across regions, but the transcript never explicitly states how a Contact is identified in the system (no contact number or ID mentioned) -- only name, email, and phone are described. Is there an actual identifier for Contact, or should Contact instead be treated as a value-type bundle keyed by (Vendor, Region)?

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.
A given vendor in a given region has exactly one primary contact.
